options.metric: Annual sum of number_of_motorist_killed, interpreted as the number of motorist deaths recorded in crash rows
options.grouping: Calendar year of crash_date, complete years 2013–2025 inclusive
options.reason: Annual motorist-death totals are the most direct outcome count available in crash records and preserve multiple deaths from a single crash.
options.answer: This crash file cannot determine whether per-mile motorist-death risk declined; recorded motorist deaths numbered 110 in 2013, peaked at 139 in 2020, and numbered 81 in 2025.
options.interpretation: The crash file cannot answer whether risk per mile declined, but the chart shows annual recorded motorist-death counts. It sums number_of_motorist_killed across all police-reported NYC crash rows and groups by calendar crash year for complete years 2013–2025, with no denominator: the count was 110 in 2013, 139 in 2020, and 81 in 2025. This is a defensible description of recorded fatality burden, while leaving per-mile risk unanswered because the file contains no miles-driven exposure. Checks found 2,132,218 rows in the planned years, 0 missing crash dates, and 0 missing motorist-death values, so all planned-year rows were retained without differential counting; all planned years are full calendar years, and partial 2026 coverage is outside the selected period.

options.metric: Annual count of crash rows where number_of_motorist_killed is greater than zero; each qualifying crash row counts once
options.denominator: None; annual count of qualifying crash rows
options.grouping: Calendar year of crash_date, complete years 2013–2025 inclusive
options.reason: Counting fatal crash events once gives a complementary view of how often reported crashes involved a motorist death, regardless of deaths per event.
options.answer: This crash file cannot determine whether per-mile motorist-death risk declined; crashes with at least one recorded motorist death numbered 102 in 2013, peaked at 126 in both 2020 and 2021, and numbered 75 in 2025.
options.interpretation: The crash file cannot answer whether risk per mile declined, but the chart shows annual counts of crash rows involving a motorist death. For police-reported NYC crashes with a known nonnegative motorist-death count in complete calendar years 2013–2025, it counts a row once when number_of_motorist_killed is greater than zero, regardless of how many motorists died in that crash; the count was 102 in 2013, 126 in both 2020 and 2021, and 75 in 2025. This is a defensible measure of fatal crash-event frequency, but it leaves per-mile risk unanswered because miles driven are not recorded. Checks found 2,132,218 rows in the planned years, 0 missing crash dates, and 0 missing or negative motorist-death values, so no rows were excluded for missing or invalid values; zero-death crashes do not qualify by definition, all planned years are full calendar years, and partial 2026 coverage is outside the selected period.
